location: Doc comments on every function; devs/deviations/skipped all make([]T,0) so none can serialize as null; scanErr unwrapped only where it terminates, errors.As used for fs.PathError. Note: workflowDeviations is now 14 hand-written comparison stanzas (61 lines), gocyclo 25 - over this repo's own 22 threshold, which no gate measures - and nothing binds its list to model.WorkflowOverride's 17 fields.

TestWorkflowDeviations_AuditConvergeOn covers all four arms (differ, illegal-but-comparable, equal, project-unset) and mirrors the review_converge_on and commit_strategy tests exactly. No bare nil slices, no TODO, helpers iptr/sptr reused rather than redeclared.

Manifest is well-formed and version is 0.36.1, deliberately behind the 0.37.0 it briefly carried: 35a9d0f4 measured the session-start hook exiting 2 against this tree's own binary at a 0.37.0 floor. Nothing in this role's domain is defective. Reminder only: the pre-release checklist still requires the bump to 0.37.0 before the tag.

Both tests are in package cli so they reach parseAuditRows directly; the rejection test asserts every offending line is named at once, which is the round-trip property the type exists for. Minor: it asserts lines 1 and 3 are named but never that line 2 (the legal 'security' row) is not, so a message naming every line would pass.

by_severity is built in the existing by_status/by_role loop and calls engine.AuditSeverityBucket rather than restating the classifier, so §2 and §4 cannot drift. Doc comments complete; rows/inputs/unique all make()'d. Ran the uncovered path: a file with a skipped malformed line and a lowercase 'pass' status still gives sum(by_severity) == findings == 3.

Strong shape: blockingAndAdvisory derives the expected counts by calling engine.AuditRowsClean rather than writing numerals beside the fixture, the four unrecognised shapes are counted out of the fixture with require.Len(shapes,4) instead of asserted in prose, and both the -o branch and the dedup population carry a recorded measurement of the variant that survived without them.

Three advisory rows rather than one, so the asserted numeral cannot be confused with the round ordinal or required_clean_rounds; mixed warning/info severities so a per-severity special case cannot pass. Both sinks driven from one helper. The empty-round strings are pinned verbatim as consts, which is what makes NotEqual a real discriminator.

Doc comments on every function and type; the wfPre-vs-wf split is justified in place and correct (nothing above the ValidAuditConvergeOn check writes). Two notes: parseAuditRows names its returns and then shadows err at line 293 while returning explicitly, so the naming buys nothing; and runAuditRecord grew 109->141 lines and runAuditStatus 107->129 this release - 27 of 32 added lines are comment, and the funlen baseline cannot see either.

The auditRecord helper pins TP_UNATTENDED off through runTPFence rather than inheriting it, with the measurement that motivated it recorded in the comment - the right fix for a suite whose own gate runs under TP_UNATTENDED=1. StoredFindingsFollowTheSharedPredicate derives `want` from engine.AuditRowIsPass and then require.Equal(5) on it, so the fixture cannot silently stop discriminating.

signalFieldKeys is named once so presence and absence assertions cannot drift; the raw-JSON assertions on `"role_streaks": []` and `"spec_coverage_clean_rounds": null` are exactly the nil-slice guard this repo needs. TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate asserts the reversed write RESOLVES rather than merely exits 0, and asserts the fixture carries no severity so the fail-closed rule is what grades it.
